question: When resistors are connected in parallel combination, then resultant resistance will be:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Less than least resistance__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Resistors are said to be connected together in “**Parallel**” when both of their terminals are respectively connected to each terminal of the other resistor or resistors.
 
• There are two paths available for **Current**.
 
• Hence current divides, but the voltage across the resistors is the same.
 
• If the two resistors are equal the current will divide equally and the R-total will be exactly half of either resistor or exactly **one-third** if there are three equal resistors.

(1)/(R_eq)= (1)/(R) + (1)/(R) 

(1)/(R_eq)= (2)/(R)

R_eq= (R)/(2)

Hence, Equivalent resistance in a parallel connected resistor combination is always less than the least resistance.
